ILLEGAL MINING TAKE DOWN

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
we give you a fly the wall look at an intelligence driven operation bringing down syndicates driving large scale illegal mining

Unique Selling Point:
** CRIMINALS GET WHAT’s COMING TO THEM
** A CB EXCLUSIVE RIDE-A-LONG
** EXCITING FOOTAGE!!!

Summary:
In July 2021 we showed viewers the extent of large scale illegal mining in Limpopo. But theses syndicates are in no way limited to that province. They are a law unto themselves – brazen illegal mining operations continue unabated - day in and day out – across the country.

We head to the North West province this time where an intelligence driven investigation is about to grab these criminals in the act in a multi-disciplinary operation like we’ve rarely, if ever, seen in South Africa.

Carte Blanche gets an exclusive ride-a-long. Buckle up – it’s gonna be an exhilarating one!


Further information:
BACKGROUND
The South African Mining Sector is under attack by criminal elements ranging from low level zama-zamas, to business forums demanding their cut of projects and jobs, to organised syndicates running illegal mining operations using big scale equipment. Chrome mines are targeted by groups who present themselves as legitimate operators extracting chrome and selling it to export market as if they have rights to land.

THE NORTH WEST CASE STUDY
In months long intelligence driven investigation is about to come together in a collaborative bust to take down three different illegal operators who have been pillaging a chrome mine in the North West. There is extensive evidence – from drone footage to undercover operatives who have infiltrated these groups to authorised agents doing mandated buys of stolen chrome.

The mine’s private security contractor has driven this investigation linking vehicles on the mine to suspects with video evidence, agent affidavits and cellphone analysis.

THE OPERATION
The Air Force, SANDF, SAPS, HAWKS teams and private security will be running an elaborate operations. We’re talking , drones that will scout the area with teams monitoring it live, troops and cops will get onto the mine in trucks pretending to be part of the mining operations, cellphone jammers will be used to block the criminal scouts getting warning outs and at least three choppers that will swoop in.

They are aiming for next week Thursday.

HOW DO WE TELL IT?
We start the piece by looking at the phenomenon of illegal mining – particularly in the area, we ID the suspects and we outline the challenges – often local cops are involved and when there is the occasional operation, not all the key criminal roleplayers are nabbed. We focus on the operation – this time round, it’s cops from outside of the area that will be blocking all exits and essentially trapping the crooks on the mine.

WHY DO IT?
Did I mention drones, choppers and an elaborate bust? But also, I think we go through so much as South Africans with all the doom and gloom and useless government departments that seeing the authorities succeed will give the country a glimmer of hope.

May need an extra day's shoot.

STRUCTURE: ILLEGAL MINING TAKE DOWN
PART ONE

VO: Illegal Mining is evolving – forget low level zama-zamas

VISUAL MOMENT

VO: Think organised syndicates with big money and big machinery.

ERROL: we are speaking about billions of rands of leakage out of our economy. this is just absolutely organized crime.

VO: Last year we reported on opportunistic groups illegally mining in Limpopo. Now, we’re honing in on criminal operations in the North West Province.

This exclusive drone footage shows what appears to be a legitimate mining operation – with labourers, excavators and side tipper trucks running at full steam – but, it’s NOT.

This is industrial scale pilfering by syndicates posing as legitimate operators, extracting and selling tonnes of chrome as if they owned the mining rights.

ERROL: //In some ways maybe this is a state capture

VO: Errol Smart is from the Minerals Council, representing the mining industry.

ERROL: We’re speaking about entire container ships leaving South Africa full of illegal minerals. //the people of South Africa own the minerals. And what's happening is some people are extracting value, that the state doesn't get the royalties, the government doesn't get the taxes.

VO: Waal de Waal heads up private security for the affected North West chrome mine.

WAAL: This is hard core criminals. This is called mine hijacking. They physically hijacked a mine.

VO: The chrome is impossible to trace - making it difficult to identify as stolen once it’s worked into legitimate markets. The criminals, who are highly organised and have so far managed to avoid arrest, know this.

LINK: But their days are numbered – an intelligence driven investigation has been underway for months drawing in multi-disciplinary teams for a next level take down that’s rarely if ever been seen in South Africa.

WAAL: this operation you can’t do with normal guards. This is a specialized operation.// That's where you've got the expertise. That's where we've got less red tape.

VO: A collaborative investigation - built on drone surveillance, vehicle recognition and operations to infiltrate the syndicates and purchase stolen chrome - has finally paid off.

WAAL: We used high tech technology. We used analyzing information. We recruit the right people amongst them. // we’ve identified the four ringleaders.


VO:
The illegal enterprise has quickly grown and over a few months as many as 40 excavators have been spotted, leaving a trail of devastation.

It’s a profitable illicit business – with this high grade chrome selling for between R950 and R1200 a ton. With a 32 ton truck fetching a minimum of R30 000 and at least 35 trucks being filled each day, the syndicates are making well over a R1 million a day for chrome they don’t actually own.

HENNIE: These crimes are committed in secrecy if it’s not stopped these criminals will continue with impunity.

VO: Brigadier Hennie Flynn is from the HAWKS in the North West.

HENNIE: these criminals normally regroup and they come back in a more strategized and organized approach.

VO: With no regard for the law, they brazenly carry on in the face of attempts to disrupt their operations. Without the kingpins being nabbed, these efforts are often little more than catch and release exercises.

HENNIE: // it's imperative for us to deal with the whole value chain and not just address, the foot soldiers that are conducting these criminal activities at the ground level. We need to deal with the facilitators, individuals that are behind the procuring and providing of the equipment/

VO: By joining forces with private security, Brigadier Flynn has been able to build significant evidence and plan a next level operation.

HENNIE: Numerous individuals were identified to be part of the activities.
WAAL: maximum people, short notice! we need to stay out of their ears and eyes, cell phone area because one cell phone call and this whole operation is off.

VO: After weeks of operational planning, it was all systems go and Carte Blanche got an exclusive opportunity to ride-along.

LINK: We are here at an undisclosed location. I still don't know where we are or where we going, but the team has been briefed and the targets have been located.

LEON: The purpose of this mission is to catch those operators.

VO: The Air Force, the police Special Task Force, police Airwing, the HAWKS and BidVEst Protea Coin’s tactical teams are all key to this elaborate operation. Choppers ready to swoop, armed personnel deployed at the mine and its perimeters ready to trap the crooks while drones monitor the area.

WAAL: So this gives live footage to the special force task force commander to execute this operation up to a second.
MAC: So what are these people doing?
WAAL: It's potential investors.

HENNIE: our focus will definitely be to arrest the main perpetrators and then obviously to seize all the equipment that they are using to gather the chrome and to remove it from the affected area.

WAAL: Because of the terrain, we've got nine helicopters. We've got two of the South African Defence Force, four of the South African police, and three of the private sector
MA: Waal are you optimistic about today?
WAAL: I am very optimistic. If you look around you with these resources, this is going to be the end of these criminals.

VO: These are specialist teams with tactical expertise usually reserved for high level operations - seeing them in action is rare.

LINK: We’re almost getting ready to go to the illegal Mining site. It doesn't happen often in South Africa. Where you’ve got all of these disciplines working together. I think today. This site is going to. Get closed down.

SHOTS OF CHOPPERS IN FORMATION // SPECIAL FORCES IN THE CHOPPERS ABOUT TO JUMP

LEON: Okay. You guys ready on that side?
PILOT: Ready to rock and roll.
LEON: Copy that.

VO: As the choppers move in, word gets out on the ground.

CROOK: eh,eh, eh,JOH! Let me run – things are looking bad here this side.

VO: This cellphone video is captured by one of the illegal miners as the operation gets underway.

CROOK: Things are not good here – there’s about four choppers this side , helicopters –OOOOH! Police!

VO: But he has no idea just how bad things are about to get.




 
PART TWO

VO:
Large Scale Illegal Mining syndicates have overrun a chrome mine in the North West Province. But a next level, collaborative bust is underway - involving the police special task force, its airwing, the Airforce, the HAWKS and private security air and ground teams.


Buckle up - it’s about to go down. And WE have a front row seat to the action - flying in with Waal de Waal from BidVest Protea Coin who runs the mine’s security operations.

LINK: All the helicopters are now going to be flying at a low level, getting into the right formation.We’re getting close to the mine right now.

VISUALS UPSOUND - GUYS IN ORYX - GOPRO

PILOT: Okay. Turning into the target now.

LINK: The first helicopter that's going to go in is going to be the Oryx from the military. And we're going to be watching, some of the members are going to be descending from their helicopter, securing the place.

VISUAL - ORYX GUYS DROPPING DOWN - GOPRO & DRONE FOOTAGE

VO: Illegal miners scatter, trying to escape arrest.

VISUAL - ORYX GUYS DROPPING DOWN - GOPRO & DRONE FOOTAGE

VO: But the teams close in from all directions. Special Task Force Members literally hitting the ground running.

From the air, we spot a Mercedes Benz - identified earlier by the drone operator. The driver is trying to flee.

WAAL: There’s a motorbike here!

VO: The motorbike races head on towards the vehicle.

OTHER PILOT: Did they stop that car?
PILOT: Yah, they did stop it. There’s a motorbike with it, so it’s fine..

VO: But the suspect is seen trying to make another run for it.

MAC: He’s trying to get away! He’s trying to get away! He’s trying to get away.






VO: But not on this biker’s watch - he moves in front of the car - blocking its escape as a police chopper comes in low with back up.

At the operational command centre, teams are being directed to different scenes - all unfolding at once - with troops dropping down from choppers and apprehending suspects. Drivers, buyers and investors are detained - no one is being spared.

VISUAL MOMENT

VO: Back in the air, we see a Fortuner trying to make a desperate getaway.

MAC: There they are! There they Are!

VO:
The focus of this operation isn’t the low level workers - the main goal is to nab the ring leaders - the money men funding the illegal mining and the buyers fuelling the demand.

Waal: We’re going to land here - just hover here.
PILOT: ….yah the police chopper, any police chopper that can come towards us
WAAL Oh! Through the gate

VISUAL MOMENT

[sub-title on screen]
Waal: Okay! There’s a police vehicle – follow him, follow him, follow him

VO: The police are giving chase in an unmarked vehicle, while air support comes in to give back up.

[whole section sub-title on screen]
PILOT: Which side is it? Is it your side?
RADIO: There he goes! There he goes!

RADIO: There he goes! There he goes!
he’s coming towards you, you need to intercept him.
MAC: He;s tryig to get away, he’s running through the township now – but we’ve got him, we’ve got him, we’ve got him.

VO 5: The driver fires shots at the cops - but in a spectacular effort from the ground team and two
support choppers - the car is brought to a halt in the middle of an informal settlement next to the mine.

LEON: Copy that. You arrested the fortunater. Copy That.

VO 5: The teams are cleaning up fast, apprehending suspects all over the mine - even the ones fleeing on foot.

MAC: Remember the one wearing the red shirt. There they are. There they are!

VO: This suspect jumps the fence thinking he is in the clear, but his freedom will be short lived.

LINK: // I don't understand why he just doesn't give up, because he's surrounded by 3-8 helicopters, people on the ground, beneath the ground, as well as the army. And it's just one man. And I don't know what he's running.

PILOT: //we’ve got the visuals.
PILOT: I’ve got him [sub-title on screen]

WIMPIE: Happy so far?
WALL: Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. I’m, happy! happy! [sub-title on screen]

LINK: Oh, man, what a rush. As you can see from the aerial view, this car, this excavators,. This is now an active crime scene.

VO: The suspects are facing possible fines and even jail time because of the scale of the unlawful activity.

With millions of rands worth of equipment scattered across the target area, the HAWKS comb the mine securing evidence.

Many of the drivers simply abandon trucks full of chrome or leave excavators standing in deep cavities.

HENNIE: hier’s ‘n celphone, - ek sien nie ‘n sleutel hier nie. [sub-title on screen]

VO: But this isn’t going to deter the cops - they call in technicians to assist in moving these exhibits off site to a secure holding area.

Thinking the scene has been contained, we’re surprised to hear an excavator starting up.

LINK: This guy over here thought he could get away and waited for everyone to go and wanted to take the excavator quickly and escape with a it, but they’ve caught him as well. M8

VO: Well over 100 million Rand’s worth of equipment is seized. Eleven trucks, two diesel tankers, four private vehicles, at least 20 excavators and illegally-mined chrome valued at more than R2 million are confiscated. Not bad for a day’s work.

MAC: So Brigadier, good day at the office. Happy with how it played out?
HENNIE: Yeah, we are happy. We are happy, Mac. I think we've done exceptionally well. The operation was executed according to plan.
MAC: Would you say you'd like to do more operations like this?
HENNIE: // most definitely, because it has its value in terms of neutralizing the threat M3M4

VO: Two of the main kingpins have been arrested, while a number of foot soldiers are now witnesses.

And as the dust settles on the illegal mining area, there’s a sense of optimism in the air..

MAC: // it was a beauty to watch// almost like a rugby game, each one passing the ball to the next as we were going down, grabbing the guys, taking them through. Is this what needs to happen for us to maybe get a hold on crime in this country?
WAAL: This is exactly what needs to happen going forward. And this is the beginning. This is the ice breaker for fighting crime going forward for this country. W3M2
MAC: oom Waal, Slaan it hier! Slaan it hier!

metadata.Unique Selling Point: ** CRIMINALS GET WHAT’s COMING TO THEM ** A CB EXCLUSIVE RIDE-A-LONG ** EXCITING FOOTAGE!!!
metadata.Summary: In July 2021 we showed viewers the extent of large scale illegal mining in Limpopo. But theses syndicates are in no way limited to that province. They are a law unto themselves – brazen illegal mining operations continue unabated - day in and day out – across the country. We head to the North West province this time where an intelligence driven investigation is about to grab these criminals in the act in a multi-disciplinary operation like we’ve rarely, if ever, seen in South Africa. Carte Blanche gets an exclusive ride-a-long. Buckle up – it’s gonna be an exhilarating one!
metadata.Further information: BACKGROUND The South African Mining Sector is under attack by criminal elements ranging from low level zama-zamas, to business forums demanding their cut of projects and jobs, to organised syndicates running illegal mining operations using big scale equipment. Chrome mines are targeted by groups who present themselves as legitimate operators extracting chrome and selling it to export market as if they have rights to land. THE NORTH WEST CASE STUDY In months long intelligence driven investigation is about to come together in a collaborative bust to take down three different illegal operators who have been pillaging a chrome mine in the North West. There is extensive evidence – from drone footage to undercover operatives who have infiltrated these groups to authorised agents doing mandated buys of stolen chrome. The mine’s private security contractor has driven this investigation linking vehicles on the mine to suspects with video evidence, agent affidavits and cellphone analysis. THE OPERATION The Air Force, SANDF, SAPS, HAWKS teams and private security will be running an elaborate operations. We’re talking , drones that will scout the area with teams monitoring it live, troops and cops will get onto the mine in trucks pretending to be part of the mining operations, cellphone jammers will be used to block the criminal scouts getting warning outs and at least three choppers that will swoop in. They are aiming for next week Thursday. HOW DO WE TELL IT? We start the piece by looking at the phenomenon of illegal mining – particularly in the area, we ID the suspects and we outline the challenges – often local cops are involved and when there is the occasional operation, not all the key criminal roleplayers are nabbed. We focus on the operation – this time round, it’s cops from outside of the area that will be blocking all exits and essentially trapping the crooks on the mine. WHY DO IT? Did I mention drones, choppers and an elaborate bust? But also, I think we go through so much as South Africans with all the doom and gloom and useless government departments that seeing the authorities succeed will give the country a glimmer of hope.
